author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of the corruption of Nature and the efficacy of Divine Grace

notes.text: (1) Romans vii. 12, 22. 25. (2) Romans vii. 18. (3) Philippians iv. 13. (4) 2 Corinthians xii. 9.

verses.text: O Lord my God, who hast created me after thine own image and similitude, grant me this grace, which Thou hast shown to be so great and so necessary for salvation, that I may conquer my wicked nature, which draweth me to sin and to perdition.
verses.modernizedText: O Lord my God, who created me after Your own image and likeness, grant me this grace, which You have shown to be so great and so necessary for salvation, so that I may conquer my wicked nature, which draws me to sin and perdition.

verses.text: For I feel in my flesh the law of sin, contradicting the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the obedience of sensuality in many things; nor can I resist its passions, unless Thy most holy grace assist me, fervently poured into my heart.
verses.modernizedText: For I feel in my flesh the law of sin, opposing the law of my mind and bringing me into captivity to obedience to sensuality in many things; nor can I resist its passions unless Your most holy grace helps me, fervently poured into my heart.

verses.text: There is need of Thy grace, yea, and of a great measure thereof, that my nature may be conquered, which hath alway been prone to evil from my youth.
verses.modernizedText: I need Your grace, and a great measure of it, so that my nature, which has always been prone to evil from my youth, may be conquered.

verses.text: For being fallen through the first man Adam, and corrupted through sin, the punishment of this stain descended upon all men; so that Nature itself, which was framed good and right by Thee, is now used to express the vice and infirmity of corrupted Nature; because its motion left unto itself draweth men away to evil and to lower things.
verses.modernizedText: For having fallen through the first man Adam and been corrupted through sin, the punishment of this stain descended upon all people; so that Nature itself, which You made good and right, is now used to express the vice and weakness of corrupted Nature, because its movement, left to itself, draws people away to evil and lower things.

verses.text: For the little power which remaineth is as it were one spark lying hid in the ashes.
verses.modernizedText: For the little power that remains is like one spark lying hidden in the ashes.

verses.text: This is Natural reason itself, encompassed with thick clouds, having yet a discernment of good and evil, a distinction of the true and the false, though it be powerless to fulfil all that it approveth, and possess not yet the full light of truth, nor healthfulness of its affections.
verses.modernizedText: This is Natural reason itself, surrounded by thick clouds, yet still able to discern good and evil and distinguish true from false, though it is powerless to fulfill all that it approves and does not yet possess the full light of truth or health in its affections.

verses.text: Hence it is, O my God, that I delight in Thy law after the inward man,(1) knowing that Thy commandment is holy and just and good; reproving also all evil, and the sin that is to be avoided: yet with the flesh I serve the law of sin, whilst I obey sensuality rather than reason.
verses.modernizedText: Thus it is, O my God, that I delight in Your law after the inward man,(1) knowing that Your commandment is holy and just and good, and reproving all evil and the sin that is to be avoided; yet with the flesh I serve the law of sin, obeying sensuality rather than reason.

verses.text: Hence it is that to will to do good is present with me, but how to perform it I find not.(2) Hence I ofttimes purpose many good things; but because grace is lacking to help mine infirmities, I fall back before a little resistance and fail.
verses.modernizedText: Thus the will to do good is present with me, but I do not find how to perform it.(2) Thus I often purpose many good things; but because grace is lacking to help my weaknesses, I fall back and fail at a little resistance.

verses.text: Hence it cometh to pass that I recognize the way of perfectness, and see very clearly what things I ought to do; but pressed down by the weight of my own corruption, I rise not to the things which are more perfect.
verses.modernizedText: Thus it happens that I recognize the way of perfection and see very clearly what I ought to do; but pressed down by the weight of my own corruption, I do not rise to the more perfect things.

verses.text: Oh how entirely necessary is Thy grace to me, O Lord, for a good beginning, for progress, and for bringing to perfection.
verses.modernizedText: Oh, how entirely necessary Your grace is to me, O Lord, for a good beginning, for progress, and for bringing things to perfection.

verses.text: For without it I can do nothing, but I can do all things through Thy grace which strengtheneth me.(3) O truly heavenly grace, without which our own merits are nought, and no gifts of Nature at all are to be esteemed.
verses.modernizedText: For without it I can do nothing, but I can do all things through Your grace which strengthens me.(3) O truly heavenly grace, without which our own merits are nothing and no gifts of Nature are to be esteemed.

verses.text: Arts, riches, beauty, strength, wit, eloquence, they all avail nothing before Thee, O Lord, without Thy grace.
verses.modernizedText: Arts, riches, beauty, strength, wit, eloquence—all are of no avail before You, O Lord, without Your grace.

verses.text: For the gifts of Nature belong to good and evil alike; but the proper gift of the elect is grace—that is, love—and they who bear the mark thereof are held worthy of everlasting life.
verses.modernizedText: For the gifts of Nature belong to good and evil alike; but the proper gift of the elect is grace—that is, love—and those who bear its mark are held worthy of everlasting life.

verses.text: So mighty is this grace, that without it neither the gift of prophecy nor the working of miracles, nor any speculation, howsoever lofty, is of any value at all.
verses.modernizedText: So mighty is this grace that without it neither the gift of prophecy nor the working of miracles nor any speculation, however lofty, is of any value.

verses.text: But neither faith, nor hope, nor any other virtue is accepted with Thee without love and grace.
verses.modernizedText: But neither faith, nor hope, nor any other virtue is accepted by You without love and grace.

verses.text: O most blessed grace that makest the poor in spirit rich in virtues, and renderest him who is rich in many things humble in spirit, come Thou, descend upon me, fill me early with Thy consolation, lest my soul fail through weariness and drought of mind.
verses.modernizedText: O most blessed grace, which makes the poor in spirit rich in virtues and makes the person rich in many things humble in spirit, come, descend upon me, fill me early with Your consolation, lest my soul fail through weariness and dryness of mind.

verses.text: I beseech thee, O Lord, that I may find grace in Thy sight, for Thy grace is sufficient for me,(4) when I obtain not those things which Nature longeth for.
verses.modernizedText: I ask You, O Lord, that I may find grace in Your sight, for Your grace is sufficient for me,(4) when I do not obtain the things Nature longs for.

verses.text: If I be tempted and vexed with many tribulations, I will fear no evil, while Thy grace remaineth with me.
verses.modernizedText: If I am tempted and vexed with many troubles, I will fear no evil while Your grace remains with me.

verses.text: This alone is my strength, this bringeth me counsel and help.
verses.modernizedText: This alone is my strength; this brings me counsel and help.

verses.text: It is more powerful than all enemies, and wiser than all the wise men in the world.
verses.modernizedText: It is more powerful than all enemies and wiser than all the wise people in the world.

verses.text: It is the mistress of truth, the teacher of discipline, the light of the heart, the solace of anxiety, the banisher of sorrow, the deliverer from fear, the nurse of devotion, the drawer forth of tears.
verses.modernizedText: It is the mistress of truth, the teacher of discipline, the light of the heart, the comfort of anxiety, the banisher of sorrow, the deliverer from fear, the nurse of devotion, the one who draws forth tears.

verses.text: What am I without it, save a dry tree, a useless branch, worthy to be cast away!
verses.modernizedText: What am I without it but a dry tree, a useless branch, worthy to be cast away!

verses.text: “Let Thy grace, therefore, O Lord, always prevent and follow me, and make me continually given to all good works, through Jesus Christ, Thy Son.
verses.modernizedText: “Let Your grace, therefore, O Lord, always go before and follow me, and make me continually devoted to all good works, through Jesus Christ, Your Son.

verses.text: Amen.”
verses.modernizedText: Amen.”
